label: prop:q-beta-q-eq-one-shadow-gate
title: $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ precision-ladder $\S 4(c)$ formalize-first gate — any candidate Habiro element $F(q)$ must reproduce the canonical integer shadows at $q = 1$: $c_2 \to -1$ (the structural N=2 anchor) and $c_3 \to J_{\text{Hopf}}(1) = -2$ (registry anchor); a candidate failing either is structurally REFUTED
html:
Proposition. \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \S 4(c) formalize-first gate — any candidate Habiro element F(q) must reproduce the canonical integer shadows at q = 1: c_2 \to -1 (the structural N=2 anchor) and c_3 \to J_{\text{Hopf}}(1) = -2 (registry anchor); a candidate failing either is structurally REFUTED

Any candidate Habiro element F(q) generating the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladder must satisfy the classical-limit shadows \lim_{q \to 1} c_2(q) = -1 and \lim_{q \to 1} c_3(q) = -2. A candidate failing either shadow is structurally REFUTED.

This enforces the q=1 shadow formalize-first gate. The seed c_2 = -1 is Taylor-exact for the explicit-factor product \prod_{k\ge2}(1 + c_k u^k) — the normalised series (cosine factor inside) has \tilde c_2 = c_2 - 1/8 = -9/8, so the series must be named. The term c_3 \to -2 is the canonical Hopf-Jones limit. A candidate whose Taylor expansion disagrees with either anchor fails this invariant.
